biography.plain_text: Paolo Radici (1946–2024) was an Italian industrialist who guided parts of his family's manufacturing group through international growth and materials diversification. A longtime shareholder and director, he oversaw Belgian carpet-printing and polyester activities. He later pursued viticulture with Lara Imberti, establishing an organic Franciacorta producer that became his second defining enterprise.

long_biography.plain_text:
Factory-floor experience shaped Radici's education while he was still studying, and journeys with his father Gianni introduced him to overseas markets. In 1977, he relocated to Belgium to establish Ralux, serving a dense cluster of European carpet manufacturers. Responsibility for polyester followed as the enterprise broadened from textiles into chemical intermediates, polymers, engineering plastics and technical fibres. With brothers Angelo and Maurizio, he helped steward the established family platform across more than five decades.

The vineyard project began in 1996 near Adro, where he and Lara Imberti restored a historic estate and replanted its slopes. Ronco Calino developed into a specialist organic sparkling-wine business rooted in Franciacorta's local traditions. After Radici's death, Imberti continued the cellar's work with its established team.
